section.title: Find the Line Parallel to a Given Line
section.para: In this section, you will use what you know about writing the equation of a line given the slope and a point to write the equation of parallel lines. The graph shows the equation of the line \( y = 2x - 3. \) The point \( P \) \( (-2, 1) \) is also plotted. You can use the fact that parallel lines have the same slope to find a line that is parallel to line \(m\) and goes through point \( P \) \( (-2, 1) \).

section.para: From the equation, you know the slope of the line is 2. The second line will pass through \( (-2, 1) \) and have slope 2. To graph the line, start at \( (-2, 1) \) and count out the rise and run. The slope is \( \frac{rise}{run}=\frac{2}{1} \). Count out the rise, 2, and run, 1, and plot the point. You can graph the line as shown. Line \( m \) is parallel to line \( l \) and goes through point \( P \) \( (-2, 1) \).

section.para: To find the equation of a line parallel to a line through a given point algebraically, you can use what you know about finding the equation of a line given the slope and a point.
Write an equation of a line parallel to \( y = 2x - 3 \) that contains the point \( (-2, 1) \). Write the equation in slope-intercept form.

Step 1 - Find the slope of the given line.
The line is in slope-intercept form \( y = 2x - 3 \)
\( m=2 \)

Step 2 - Find the slope of the parallel line
Parallel lines have the same slope
\( m_1 = 2 \)

Step 3 - Identify the point
The given point is \( (-2, 1) \)
\( (x_1, y_1) = (-2, 1) \)

Step 4 - Substitute values into the point-slope form \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \)
Simplify
\(\begin{array}{rcl}y-y_1&=&(x-x_1)\\y-1&=&(x-(-2))\\y-1&=&(x+2)\\y-1&=&x+4\end{array}\)

Step 5 - Write the equation in slope-intercept form
\( y = 2x + 5 \)
Look at the graph with the parallel lines shown previously. Does this equation make sense? What is the \(y\)-intercept of the line? What is the slope?
You can use this table as a reference for writing an equation of a line parallel to a given line.

section.title: Try It: Find the Line Parallel to a Given Line

problem.para: Write an equation of a line parallel to the line \(y = 3x + 1\) that contains the point \( (4,2) \). Write the equation in slope-intercept form.
Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to find a line parallel to a given line and point.

Step 1 - Find the slope of the given line.
\( m = 3 \)

Step 2 - Find the slope of the parallel line.
\( m_1 = 3 \)

Step 4 - Substitute the values into the point-slope form: \( y-y_1=m(x-x_1) \).
\(\begin{array}{rcl}y-y_1&=&m(x-x_1)\\y-2&=&3(x-4)\end{array}\)

Step 6 - Write the equation in slope-intercept form: \( y = mx+b \).
\( y = 3x - 10 \)
